ERNA

ERNA gold and silversmith

Skipholt 3, Reykjavík founded 3 February 1924

THE THINGS that mark an ICELANDIC LIFE

The christening spoon. The engagement ring. The wedding fork. The graduation star. The Christmas spoon, collected one a year for decades. These are not products. They are the objects Icelandic families hand down, and the workshop that makes them has stood at Skipholt 3 since Guðlaugur A. Magnússon founded it in 1924.

See the work

WHAT gets handed DOWN

Five objects. Five moments in one life. All hand made in Skipholt.

The first silver

The christening spoon

Since 1936 ERNA’s silversmiths have hand made Icelandic children’s spoons in silver. Five motifs are still in production: the clock, the child, the swan, Red Riding Hood, and Hansel and Gretel.

Engagement and wedding rings

Domed 3 mm bands in 14 carat gold, hand forged in the Skipholt workshop. The price is for the pair, engraving included. Wider profiles, diamonds and tantalum are also available.

The first meal

The wedding fork

The couple eat from it together, as a sign of shared minds and equal footing. Hand made in solid silver, from the Faber Islandicus line. The couple’s initials can be engraved on the heart.

ISK 37,500Hand engraving from ISK 1,500 per character.

The cap

The graduation star

The star on a long chain, in silver or 14 carat gold. It is given on the day the white cap goes on, and it tends not to come off afterwards.

ISK 14,500 in silverISK 69,500 in 14 carat gold.

One a year

The Christmas spoon

It is 79 years since the first Christmas spoon was made at ERNA, in 925 sterling silver, the same way as at the start. The current series is designed by Ragnhildur Sif Reynisdóttir on a theme of music. The 2026 spoon will be the twelfth, and the last ERNA produces.

THE SILVER. the fire. THE MARK.

Three steps, unchanged for decades.

01

the silver

925

Sterling silver and nothing else. Production of Icelandic silver flatware began in the workshop in 1936, and the patterns from those years are still made: Erna, Kaktus, Renaissance, Reykjavík, Vor and Smári.

02

the fire

Hand forged

The silver is melted in the crucible and heated until it gives. What is hand made passes through hands before it passes into a box. The workshop has stood in the same place in Skipholt for decades.

03

the hallmark

One blow

At the end the punch is struck. GAM beneath a rising sun, with the fineness 925 below. That mark has been in use since 1946. After it, the object has a history that can be read.

  1. 01the silver
  2. 02the fire
  3. 03the hallmark

and the object is marked

ONE blow, and the object has a HISTORY

ERNA keeps a public register of maker’s marks: a record, smith by smith, of the Icelandic gold and silversmiths who struck their own mark into metal. The plate above is the workshop’s own test plate, struck with the smiths’ punches.

From the register

  • GAM

    Guðlaugur A. Magnússon, 1902 til 1952

    The founder’s initials beneath a rising sun, with the sterling fineness below. In use from 1946. Before that, from 1924, the mark was GAM plus a fineness stamp.

  • GB

    Guðjón Bernharðsson, 1901 til 1978

    Ran a silver workshop first in Akureyri, later in Reykjavík. In 1960 his workshop merged into Erna hf. His son Gunnar drew the Rauðhetta spoon, still sought after seven decades later.

  • SS

    Silfursmiðjan, Kornelíus Jónsson, 1915 til 2010

    SS stands for Silfursmiðjan, run by several well known watch and goldsmiths in Reykjavík. Kornelíus kept producing some of the old patterns until 2010, aged almost 95.

THE SAME family since 1924

Guðlaugur began in Ísafjörður. His son Reynir started the day after his confirmation. Today the third and fourth generation of the family are at work, and Sara Steina is managing director.

  1. 1924Guðlaugur A. Magnússon opens a workshop in Ísafjörður on 3 February.
  2. 1927The workshop moves to Reykjavík, by way of Hafnarfjörður.
  3. 1936Silver flatware production begins, the Christmas spoons among it.
  4. 1946The GAM mark beneath a rising sun, 925 below, comes into use.
  5. 1947Production becomes a company named Erna, after Jónína Erna, Guðlaugur’s daughter.
  6. 1960Guðjón Bernharðsson’s silver workshop merges into Erna hf.
  7. 2026The third and fourth generation of the family are at work in Skipholt 3.
